sentences.text: Romeosaurus is an extinct yaguarasaurine mosasaur discovered in the Lastame lithotype of northern Italy.
The species Romeosaurus sorbinii is known only from a single, very fragmented specimen and remains poorly described.
In contrast, the species Romeosaurus fumanensis is known from multiple specimens found across a small area in Italy.
Romeosaurus was a medium-sized mosasaur, comparable to Clidastes, and likely did not exceed 3 meters in length.
Like other mosasaurs, Romeosaurus had a fusiform body with limbs adapted for swimming.
No recovered specimens of Romeosaurus have well-preserved post-cranial fossils, making it difficult to determine their body anatomy beyond the skull.
The genus name Romeosaurus honors the character Romeo from Shakespeare's play, referencing the proximity of the fossil sites to Verona.
R. sorbinii differs from R. fumanensis by having a different frontal bone shape, fewer upper jaw teeth, and ornamented tooth enamel.
The genus Romeosaurus was first described by Palci and colleagues in 2013.
The species R. sorbinii is named after paleontologist Lorenzo Sorbini, while R. fumanensis is named after the town of Fumane.
As of 2018, only one specimen of R. sorbinii and four specimens of R. fumanensis were known to science.
Romeosaurus was distinguished from Russellosaurus, Tethysaurus, and Pannoniasaurus by the presence of a pre-dental rostrum in the jaw.
Research by Palci et al. supports the hypothesis that the evolution of limbs into fin-like structures occurred twice independently within mosasaurs.
Romeosaurus is classified within the subfamily Yaguarasaurinae.
Phylogenetic analysis indicates Romeosaurus is a close relative of the North American Russellosaurus and the South American Yaguarasaurus, forming the primitive subfamily Yaguarasaurinae.
Romeosaurus belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
Romeosaurus fossils date to the Late Cretaceous period.
Romeosaurus lived in northern Italy during the early Late Cretaceous, specifically between the early Turonian and early Santonian stages.
Romeosaurus fossils were recovered from the Scaglia Rossa Veneta formation, specifically the Lastame lithozone, which was an open sea environment during the Late Cretaceous.
The open marine environment of the Lastame lithozone is supported by finds of marine vertebrates like Cretoxyrhina and Ptychodus, as well as ammonites and planktonic foraminifera.
Romeosaurus lived from the Turonian to the Santonian stages, approximately 93.9 to 83.6 million years ago.
